root_cause: Postings::by_identity and Postings::by_vid (crates/tgms-engine-core/src/store.rs) are append-only identity indexes with no prune at all, unlike open_rows, which at least prunes per-lookup in read.rs::locate_open. Periodic compaction (compact.rs::compact) physically reseals every row that still exists -- open and closed, since compaction never drops one -- into fresh segments every cycle, and the next lookup (read.rs::index_segments, reached through any correction's close_version -> locate_vid) re-indexes them there, stacking on top of every earlier cycle's now-unreachable entries that nothing ever freed: entries for a superseded cycle's segments become permanently unreachable (their segment id is gone from the current file map, so locate/locate_vid/locate_open silently skip them) but were never removed from the maps themselves. This is the shared engine commit/compaction path (gc() -> evict_segments_not_in), not something specific to the replay reader: reproduced directly with a plain correction + compact()/gc() write loop (no replay involved) showing the same non-plateauing per-commit growth, and confirmed precisely via a new NativeStore::postings_stats() counter (2,190 by_identity/by_vid entries for 400 versions ever committed over 10 compaction cycles, unfixed, against a floor of ~400 fixed).

symptom: a read-only opener raised StateError("event log .../eventlog.jsonl record at offset 4076 has no terminating newline and is not the log's last record -- the replay cursor may not be on a record boundary") from tgms/storage/eventlog.py:270-275, inside EventLog.batches_from's torn-tail tolerance check.
root_cause: Distinct from D-086-reader-torn-tail-race (the JSONDecodeError-shaped race, where tolerance was correctly refused because a required gate did not hold). Here the gate's own inputs are stale: batches_from captures `raw`/`end` when it first meets a torn (non-newline-terminated) record, then re-stats the file with a fresh `size = f.seek(0, 2)` to decide whether that record is still the log's last (eventlog.py:258-259). EventLog.append's write-ahead guarantee is one write() then fsync() then return; if that single append -- completing the SAME record the reader is looking at -- lands between the reader's initial read and its size re-stat, the file has grown past the reader's stale `end`, `end >= size` now reads False, the `writer_active()` probe (the one call site D-086-reader-torn-tail-race's two-gate rule relies on) is skipped entirely, and a record that is now complete and sound on disk is reported as damage. The bug is staleness of the comparison inputs, not a missing gate: re-reading the record at its start offset before deciding 'not last' would show it is now whole.
regression_test: tests/test_reader_torn_tail_race.py::test_writer_completing_the_torn_record_between_read_and_size_check_is_not_damage (deterministic repro via a monkeypatched EventLog.batches_from that completes the torn record on disk at the exact f.seek(0, 2) call; currently xfail(strict=True) -- documents the open bug, must be updated in the same commit that fixes it). 30x re-run of the CI test on this laptop (PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_concurrency.py -k readers_opening_throughout -q): 0/30 failures -- the live race is rare (D-086-reader-torn-tail-race's own wild observations put it near 1-in-2,100 reader reopens), consistent with a single CI hit on 3.11 only.
fix_summary: EventLog.batches_from now retries once: when a torn/unparseable candidate's stale `end` is behind a freshly re-stat'd `size`, it seeks back to `start` and readline()s the record again before trusting a "not last" verdict. If the fresh read is a complete, newline-terminated, parseable record, it is yielded normally; otherwise the end>=size / writer_active decision is redone with the retry's own fresh end and a fresh size (one retry only, no loop, no sleep).
